I'll systematically compare the source and draft, hunting for signature passages that are missing or degraded.

**Key passages to check:**

1. The "secret part of the tragedy" framing — present in draft, reasonably preserved.
2. The Great Lakes passage — verbatim in draft. ✓
3. The Canaller description / "Corrupt as Lima" — verbatim. ✓
4. Steelkilt's description as "a tall and noble animal with a head like a Roman, and a flowing golden beard like the tasseled housings of your last viceroy's snorting charger; and a brain, and a heart, and a soul in him, gentlemen, which had made Steelkilt Charlemagne, had he been born son to Charlemagne's father. But Radney, the mate, was ugly as a mule" — **ABSENT** in draft. This is one of the most distinctive, quoted passages in the chapter.

5. The pump banter speech — partially preserved but significantly truncated. Source has: "I tell ye what, men, old Rad's investment must go for it! he had best cut away his part of the hull... sword-fish only began the job; he's come back again with a gang of ship-carpenters, saw-fish, and file-fish... making improvements... if old Rad were here now, I'd tell him to jump overboard... his property is invested in looking-glasses. I wonder if he'd give a poor devil like me the model of his nose." — The last part ("his property is invested in looking-glasses... model of his nose") is **ABSENT**.

6. The "stacks of powder-casks heaped up in him and the slow-match silently burning" passage — present in draft. ✓

7. The source has the captain threaten "I mean to mince ye up for the try-pots" directed at **three men** — but the draft says "the two in the rigging" — a factual error/flattening (source says three traitors hung in rigging).

8. The source passage: "Now, as you well know, it is not seldom the case in this conventional world of ours—watery or otherwise; that when a person placed in command over his fellow-men finds one of them to be very significantly his superior in general pride of manhood, straightway against that man he conceives an unconquerable dislike..." — **ABSENT** in draft. This is an interpretively significant digression.

9. Steelkilt's speech from the barricade: "'It's not our fault; we didn't want it; I told him to take his hammer away; it was boy's business... I told him not to prick the buffalo... ain't those mincing knives down in the forecastle there, men?...'" — **ABSENT/heavily compressed** in draft.

10. "And for what are you bound?" exchange — present. ✓

11. The "appalling beauty of the vast milky mass" passage — present. ✓

12. "seizing a rope, he applied it with all his might to the backs of the two traitors, till they yelled no more, but lifelessly hung their heads sideways, as the two crucified thieves are drawn" — draft has this but says "two in the rigging" instead of three.
